data.title: 44 Thais repatriated from Cambodia
data.description: Thai security authorities received 44 Thai nationals returning from Cambodia at the Ban Khlong Luek border checkpoint in Aranyaprathet district of Sa Kaeo province on Friday, with five wanted on arrest warrants.

data.title: Chiang Mai city buses returning to the roads
data.description: City buses will resume services in Chiang Mai this month, after soaring fuel prices forced the operator to pull the fleet off the streets for the first time in eight years.

data.title: Flooding persists in six provinces
data.description: Flooding continues to affect six provinces in Thailand, with more than 73,000 people impacted, while some areas have begun recovery efforts as water levels recede, according to the Department of Disaster Prevention and Mitigation (DDPM).

data.title: 600 rai of illegal durian plantations to be cleared in Trat
data.description: TRAT - Authorities are preparing to clear more than 600 rai of illegal durian plantations around the Huai Raeng reservoir in Muang district of this eastern province as part of a crackdown on encroachment by investors.

data.title: Restaurant consoles customer who left ominous order note
data.description: A restaurant owner in Thailand has shared how a seemingly innocuous note left on a food delivery order prompted him and his partner to contact a customer, who was going through an emotional crisis and had intended the meal to be her last.

data.title: Two new plant species discovered in Tak national park
data.description: Two plant species previously unknown to science have been discovered in Khun Phawo National Park in Tak province, the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation (DNP) said.

data.title: Govt urged to create task force
data.description: <p>The Pollution Control Department (PCD) is asking the Natural Resources and Environment Ministry to establish a task force to tackle industrial waste problems after finding that illegal waste disposal cases are linked across several provinces.</p>

data.title: Over 20 Taiwanese cuffed over links to scam network
data.description: <p>Thailand and Taiwan have arrested more than 20 Taiwanese suspects allegedly linked to a call-centre scam network operating in Cambodia, with investigators now trying to identify the financiers behind the operation.</p>

data.title: People's Party aiming for Nonthaburi PAO presidency
data.description: <p>The opposition People's Party (PP) has launched its campaign for the Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organisation (PAO) presidency, with candidate Decharut Sukkumnoed drawing ballot number 4 and urging residents to back him in the Sept 20 election.</p>

data.title: Thai government to review gun controls
data.description: <p>The government is preparing sweeping amendments to the country's gun control law, with the draft expected to reach the cabinet around mid-September after further public consultation, Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilprapunt says.</p>

data.title: Klatham merger 'will help Pheu Thai'
data.description: <p>Political commentator Jatuporn Prompan has warned that a possible merger between Pheu Thai and the Klatham Party could reshape the political landscape, potentially making Pheu Thai the second-largest party and challenging Bhumjaithai's position as the largest.</p>

data.title: SRT subsidiary readies for ARL takeover
data.description: <p>The State Railway of Thailand (SRT) is preparing its subsidiary to take over the Airport Rail Link when the current operator's contract ends next month.</p>

data.title: House asked to look into AoT deals
data.description: <p>Former MP Charnchai Isarasenarak and former senator Adm Phajun Tamprateep have asked the House panel tasked with budget scrutiny to investigate an Airports of Thailand Plc (AoT) board resolution to amend airport duty-free and commercial concession contracts due to projected financial losses.</p>

data.title: Moei River overflows, prompting border market vendors in Mae Sot to move goods
data.description: Continuous heavy rain caused the Moei River in Mae Sot district of Tak province to overflow on Friday morning, forcing vendors at Rim Moei market to move their goods to higher ground.

data.title: People's Party aiming for Nonthaburi PAO presidency
data.description: <p>The opposition People's Party (PP) has launched its campaign for the Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organisation (PAO) presidency, with candidate Decharut Sukkumnoed drawing ballot number 4 and urging residents to back him in the Sept 20 election.</p>

data.title: AI push spurs privacy fears
data.description: <p>The government's TH-AI Passport project, which attracted about one million registrations within two days of its pre-launch, has raised questions about how personal data will be collected, stored and used.</p>

data.title: Govt to review gun controls
data.description: <p>The government is preparing sweeping amendments to the country's gun control law, with the draft expected to reach the cabinet around mid-September after further public consultation, Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilprapunt says.</p>

data.title: DSI asks Somchart  to clarify holdings
data.description: <p>The Department of Special Investigation (DSI) has summoned People's Party (PP) MP for Phuket, Somchart Techathavorncharoen, to clarify his alleged role in companies under investigation for suspected nominee arrangements.</p>

data.title: Canva tie-up to boost sector
data.description: <p>Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas has highlighted Thailand's cooperation with Australian digital design technology company Canva as a key opportunity to strengthen the country's creative economy.</p>

data.title: Court fines Israeli man B5,000 for threat against Koh Samui zoo owner
data.description: SURAT THANI: The Koh Samui Provincial Court ordered a 5,000-baht fine on an Israeli man for making a threat against the life of a Thai woman operating a zoo on Koh Samui.

data.title: Bangkok districts to report on pink-card probe on Friday
data.description: All 50 district offices in Bangkok are due to submit preliminary findings by Friday in a probe into pink-card registration fraud, while four City Hall officials have been suspended pending further action.

data.title: Illegal Chinese-made pet food worth B30m seized
data.description: More than 68 tonnes of illegally imported dog and cat food worth over 30 million baht was seized from warehouses in Samut Prakan and Samut Sakhon following a joint crackdown on an alleged smuggling network linked to online sales.

data.title: Crusading journalist Chutima Sidasathian dies at age 44
data.description: Chutima Sidasathian, an award-winning Thai investigative journalist whose reports exposing corruption attracted relentless legal harassment from government and corporate interests, has died at the age of 44.

data.title: B1-billion money trail linked to 2021 exam fraud
data.description: The National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC) is expanding its investigation into civil service examination fraud after tracing 1 billion baht in financial transactions to a previous cheating case involving local exams in Pattaya in 2021.

data.title: Thai and Myanmar military chiefs meet in Bangkok
data.description: BANGKOK - Myanmar’s military chief met on Thursday with the chief of Thai defence forces in Bangkok in his first foreign trip since assuming the role.

data.title: Fresh rain threat looms over Nan recovery
data.description: NAN - Flood-hit areas of this northern province could face renewed danger this weekend, with another round of rain forecast for Sunday, raising concerns about landslides and flash floods as communities recover from this week’s devastating flooding.

data.title: Students injured by swarming bees
data.description: CHON BURI — Seventeen people, including 13 students, were injured after a swarm of giant honey bees attacked them near the Bang Lamung district office in Chon Buri on Thursday morning.

data.title: Din Daeng hit by two fires in one day
data.description: A residential area of Din Daeng district of Bangkok was struck by fire twice on Wednesday, with the second blaze completely destroying a house and injuring two people.

data.title: Five arrested for unlicensed dental and medical services
data.description: Consumer Protection Police have arrested five people accused of illegally providing dental and medical services in Bangkok, Samut Prakan and Samut Sakhon, seizing more than 1,000 items of medical equipment and supplies worth over 330,000 baht.

data.title: Two suspects in Chiang Rai gold shop robbery arrested in Laos
data.description: Two suspects wanted in connection with the armed robbery of a gold shop at a major shopping mall in Chiang Khong district of Chiang Rai province earlier this month have been arrested in Laos.

data.title: Clean-up begins as floods pass through Nan
data.description: NAN - Rehabilitation work is beginning in upper and central districts of this northern province as floodwaters from the overflowing Nan River move south, governor Chainarong Wongyai said on Thursday.

data.title: Samut Sakhon motorway section to open Aug 28
data.description: The Department of Highways will open a 16.4-kilometre section of the M82 elevated motorway from Ekachai to Ban Phaeo in Samut Sakhon or a trial period on Aug 28.

data.title: Exam fraud investigation reports due by Aug 31
data.description: <p>The Interior Ministry has ordered local authorities to wrap up investigations into suspected fraud in local government examinations by the end of the month, while the Anti-Money Laundering Office (Amlo) examines financial trails for possible asset seizures.</p>

data.title: Bangkok to develop sky gardens
data.description: <p>Bangkok will develop sky gardens linking two of of the city's historical landmarks, the Golden Mount and Mahakan Fort.</p>

data.title: Election Commission pressed on Senate poll case
data.description: <p>Pressure is mounting on the Election Commission (EC) after a civic network, a group of reserve senators and a former MP urged the poll regulator to send a 2024 Senate election fraud case allegedly involving 229 people to court without further delay.</p>

data.title: People’s Party questions naming of MP in nominee probe
data.description: <p>The opposition People's Party (PP) has questioned the Department of Special Investigation (DSI) over its investigation into Phuket MP Somchat Techathaworncharoen, saying the disclosure of his name before any formal charges had been filed could create the impression that he had already committed an offence.</p>

data.title: Elevated M82 section to open
data.description: The Department of Highways (DoH) will open a 16.4-kilometre section of the M82 elevated motorway from Ekachai to Ban Phaeo for a trial period on Aug 28.
